title: The Three Axes of Aircraft Motion
source: FAA PHAK, Chapter 5, pp. 5-12–5-13; Chapter 6, pp. 6-2–6-4

paragraphs.en: An airplane can rotate about three imaginary axes that intersect near its center of gravity. Each axis describes a different type of motion. The longitudinal axis runs from nose to tail, the lateral axis extends from one wingtip to the other, and the vertical axis passes through the aircraft from top to bottom.
paragraphs.zh: 飛機可以繞著三條假想軸旋轉，這三條軸在重心附近相交，各自對應不同的運動。縱軸由機鼻延伸至機尾；橫軸由一側翼尖延伸至另一側；垂直軸則貫穿機身上下。

paragraphs.en: Rotation around the longitudinal axis is called roll. The ailerons normally control this motion by creating a difference in lift between the wings. Rotation around the lateral axis is called pitch, which is primarily controlled by the elevator. Rotation around the vertical axis is called yaw, which is controlled by the rudder on a conventional airplane.
paragraphs.zh: 繞縱軸旋轉稱為滾轉（roll），一般由副翼透過兩翼升力差來控制。繞橫軸旋轉稱為俯仰（pitch），主要由升降舵控制。繞垂直軸旋轉稱為偏航（yaw），傳統飛機由方向舵控制。

paragraphs.en: These motions do not always occur independently. When the pilot rolls into a turn, adverse yaw may cause the nose to move opposite the intended direction. Coordinating the ailerons and rudder helps control this tendency. Understanding the three axes gives pilots a clear way to describe aircraft attitudes and the purpose of primary flight controls.
paragraphs.zh: 這些運動不一定彼此獨立。當機師開始滾轉進入轉彎時，逆偏航可能使機鼻朝預定方向的相反側偏移。配合使用副翼與方向舵能減少這個傾向。理解三軸運動，有助於描述飛機姿態及主要操縱面的用途。
